title: How Your Eyes Turn Light Into Sight
description: How the eye focuses light into signals for the brain and how common vision problems are, from the NIH and WHO.
narration: How does light become the picture you see? Light enters through the cornea, the clear dome at the front, which bends it to help the eye focus. The coloured iris adjusts how much light the pupil admits. The lens and cornea together focus light onto the retina, where photoreceptor cells turn it into electrical signals. Those signals travel along the optic nerve to the brain, which converts them into the image you see. The World Health Organization reports that at least 2.2 billion people worldwide have impaired near or distance vision. In at least 1 billion of those cases, the impairment could have been prevented or has not yet been addressed. Uncorrected refractive error is a leading cause of impaired vision in every country, among children and adults alike. Glasses for refractive error and cataract surgery are among the most cost-effective health-care interventions there are.

claims.quote: The lens works together with the cornea to focus light correctly on the retina. When light hits the retina (a light-sensitive layer of tissue at the back of the eye), special cells called photoreceptors turn the light into electrical signals.

claims.sentence: Those signals travel along the optic nerve to the brain, which converts them into the image you see.
claims.quote: These electrical signals travel from the retina through the optic nerve to the brain. Then the brain turns the signals into the images you see.

claims.quote: Globally, at least 2.2 billion people have a near or distance vision impairment.

claims.quote: In at least 1 billion – or almost half – of these cases, vision impairment could have been prevented or has yet to be addressed.
